The fact the you have Israeli citizenship changed everything.
As an Israeli you can’t just say the you permanently left to get you money with no tax.
You need to be approved that you are no longer considered as a taxpayer in Israel based on few requirements that you can read in the website (how long you’re out of the country, proof of residency in another country and so on)
You also need a release document from your employer (form 161 and you need to file 161a as well), then you might be able to get some of your pizuim free of tax, as for pension I’m afraid you can’t receive them free of taxes as a citizen but in some cases you might get tax reduction from MAs Hachnasa, I don’t know where you move to but some countries has amana that avoid double tax or over tax 
Since you are abroad already I would use a tax company or accountant to support you with this process.
It is important to all of us to remember: that once you are a citizen and decide to leave for good to go for Nituk toshvut process to avoid tax and other obligations as an Israeli abroad
